draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kanhangad! It's the most populous city in Kasaragod district, and its old fort is called Hosdurg, which simply means 'new fort'.
draft.hungryLine: Kanhangad has lots of places doing proper Malabar meat and fish dishes.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Hosdurg Fort is an 8 min walk, and the Nithyananda Ashram with its caves is right in town.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Ananda Ashramam has the Panchavati Garden, a raised seat under five sprawling trees that's made for daydreaming.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Nithyananda Ashram near the fort has 45 caves.

spots.name: Ananda Ashramam
spots.detail: On Mavungal Road · Gardens and a library

tips.title: Time it for theyyam.
tips.body: At the Madiyan Koolam temple, theyyam is performed during the festival in May/June and December/January.

tips.title: Stay for a lecture.
tips.body: Ananda Ashramam holds a free lecture every afternoon and offers free food to visitors.

story.title: A new fort
story.body: Somashekara Nayaka of the Keladi Nayaka dynasty built Hosdurg Fort, and the Nayaks also built the Shiva temple south-west of it.

story.title: A taluk splits
story.body: Hosdurg taluk was split into Hosdurg and Vellarikundu, with Kanhangad as Hosdurg's headquarters.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Fort walls, quiet ashrams and theyyam season. Tell me which one pulled you in.
